synopsis: ICMM is an international association of major mining companies and associations; its ICSV program brought mining companies and equipment makers together to target collision-avoidance technology availability by 2025, using EMESRT requirements and adopting EMESRT’s nine-layer model [f15612, f15613, f15614, f15615]. The ICMM–EMESRT Vehicle Interaction Leading Sites Program, published in April 2024, treats intervention as one control layer rather than a complete solution and requires understanding the effectiveness of Levels 1–7 before adding advisory Level 8 and intervention Level 9 controls [f15616, f15617, f11750, f12386]. For validation planning, the corpus calls for integration with existing site controls and scenario-based functional-performance requirements, rather than validating an automatic brake in isolation [f704, f703, f15622]. It also warns that technology can change human performance positively or negatively, and unqualified Level 9 deployment can harm production and accelerate brake wear; the booklet therefore recommends measuring nuisance braking as carefully as missed interventions [f581, f15620, f15623]. These positions are useful planning guidance, but the booklet did not review ICSV in depth and explicitly identifies verification gaps in Chapters 10, 12 and 13; the 2025 date is a stated availability goal, not evidence here that it was achieved [f15621, f2588].
